newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foreigners can put $67 bln more in Taiwan stocks.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners can put $67 bln more in Taiwan stocks.

text.p: Foreign investors can put US$67.164 billion more into Taiwan's stock market before hitting an official ceiling, the central bank said on Saturday.
As of January 8, foreign investors are allowed to invest a total of $77.451 billion in Taiwan's stock market, or 25 percent of the market's total market value, the bank said in a statement.
Foreign institutions remitted a total of $56 million into Taiwan's stock market between January 1 and 8, compared with $378 million in December, the statement said.
June's $912.968 million was the highest monthly figure in 1996, it said.
Taiwan also set a ceiling of $3 billion for funds raised overseas by local firms through convertible bonds and global depositary receipts.
In that category, foreigners as can still put $1.305 billion more into the island as of January 8, the bank said.
